analysis.one_liner: Asian Paints makes and sells decorative and industrial paints, coatings and related home-improvement products, and is India's largest paint company by sales.
analysis.whats_happening: Asian Paints will report Q2 FY27 (July-September 2026) results on October 29, 2026, when the board will also decide on an interim dividend (record date November 4, 2026 if declared). Separately, the company has sent shareholders a postal ballot (notice dated October 7, 2026) seeking approval to appoint Leo Puri as an independent director for five years from September 2026. The bigger overhang is a live Competition Commission of India probe, ordered after Grasim's Birla Opus accused Asian Paints of offering dealers exclusivity incentives to block the new entrant.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the paint brand most Indian households already know, and it has historically earned very high returns on capital with almost no debt. The tension: since 2024, Grasim (part of the Aditya Birla group) entered decorative paints as Birla Opus and undercut prices by 10-15%, and Asian Paints' market share has slipped from roughly 59% to about 52%. Recent profit growth looks strong, but a chunk of it is the business recovering from a weak year-ago quarter that was itself hit by this price war, not pure re-acceleration. The stock price has not recovered to its 2023 high even as profit has grown again.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): revenue/total income ₹10,541.94 cr (+18% YoY), PAT ₹1,559.45 cr (+39.6% YoY), EBITDA ₹2,168.76 cr (+33.5% YoY). Management (MD Amit Syngle) cited double-digit domestic decorative volume growth and a 27% jump in international sales (20.3% in constant currency). Sources differ on the exact volume/value split for domestic decorative (one cites 9% volume/16.6% value growth, another 10.9% volume/6% value) — flagged as non-reconciled, not independently resolved. Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026): PAT jumped 69.3% YoY to ₹1,172.1 cr, but this is a low-base effect — Q4 FY25 profit (~₹692 cr implied) had itself been depressed by the Birla Opus price war, so the headline jump overstates the pace of recovery versus Q4 FY24's ₹1,256 cr. FY26 full year: revenue +5.1% to ₹35,583.5 cr, PAT +17.9% to ₹4,325.4 cr — modest top-line growth with better margins.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is 30.7% below its July 2023 peak of ₹3,430. There is no demerger or bonus issue behind this fall — the 2003 and 2013 actions were simple splits, already reflected in the price series — so this is a genuine price decline, not a corporate-action artefact. It coincides with the Birla Opus entry and share loss. One-year return of +2.5% has beaten the Nifty's -9.9%, but 3-year (-21%) and 5-year (-25%) returns badly trail the Nifty (+15%, +25%) and are broadly in line with or worse than peer Berger Paints (-14.6% and -29% respectively) — the entire listed paints sector has de-rated, not just Asian Paints alone.
analysis.valuation_read: Trading near ₹2,376 against trailing EPS that implies a P/E of roughly 46x, with P/B near 10x. It is expensive mainly because the market still prices in Asian Paints eventually stabilising its market share and sustaining a ~26% ROCE once the price war cools — not because near-term growth is exceptional (FY26 revenue grew only 5.1%). Whether that premium is justified is an open question: it depends entirely on whether the 52% share floor holds or keeps eroding toward Birla Opus.
analysis.growth_read: Recent growth is a mix, tilted toward price/mix rather than pure volume. Domestic decorative volume growth of roughly 9-11% is respectable, but EBITDA is growing faster than revenue, aided by a 6-8% price hike taken from April 2026 and softer input costs — margin recovery, not a volume boom. International business (+27% YoY) is genuinely growth-led and is diversifying revenue away from the domestic price war.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk is not the concern: ROCE is 26.3%, ROE 21.8%, and debt-to-equity is just 0.05 — a near debt-free balance sheet. The real risk is business/competitive risk: sustained share loss to Birla Opus, pricing pressure, and an unresolved CCI investigation into alleged anti-competitive dealer practices that could carry financial or reputational consequences depending on its outcome.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the family promoter group) held 52.63% as of the latest disclosed quarter. Pledging is limited and scattered — around 4.97% of promoter holding, created by individual family entities (e.g., Geetanjali Trading, Satyen A. Gandhi) against business loans, with Smiti Holding having released a large pledge in August 2026 — this reads as routine financing by smaller family entities rather than group-wide stress, but it's worth watching for new disclosures. FIIs raised their stake to 13.32% (from 12.11%) while mutual funds trimmed to 10.09% (from 11.42%) in the June 2026 quarter. No marquee individual investor is disclosed on the register — none found, so none to report.
strengths: ROCE of 26.3% and ROE of 21.8% on a near debt-free balance sheet (debt-to-equity 0.05)
Q1 FY27 PAT grew 39.6% YoY to ₹1,559 cr with EBITDA up 33.5%, showing margin recovery after FY25's price-war hit
International business grew 27% YoY (20.3% in constant currency), reducing reliance on the contested domestic market
Still India's largest paint company with an estimated ~52% decorative market share despite a well-funded new entrant
watchpoints: Decorative paints market share has fallen from roughly 59% to about 52% since Birla Opus's 2024 entry, and Birla Opus has reportedly crossed 10% revenue share
An active CCI investigation into alleged abuse-of-dominance dealer incentives is unresolved and could result in penalties or forced changes to trade practices
Stock remains 30.7% below its July 2023 peak, and 3-year (-21%) and 5-year (-25%) returns have badly trailed the Nifty — no re-rating yet despite recent EPS growth
Q4 FY26's 69% profit jump was measured against a depressed Birla-Opus-affected year-ago quarter — treat it as a base-effect recovery, not confirmation the old growth trend has resumed
analysis.one_thing: The October 29, 2026 Q2 FY27 results — specifically whether domestic decorative volume growth and market share stabilise against Birla Opus — will show whether the recent margin recovery is durable or another base-effect blip.
analysis.data_notes: PAT, revenue and EBITDA figures for Q1 FY27, Q4 FY26 and full-year FY26 were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Groww, Business Standard, Upstox, Kotak Securities) and are consistent. The domestic decorative volume-vs-value growth split for Q1 FY27 varies between sources (9% volume/16.6% value vs 10.9% volume/6% value) and could not be reconciled — treat with caution. One source stated DII shareholding at 1.02%, inconsistent with another showing ~20.77%; the 1.02% figure was set aside as an outlier. P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE and debt-to-equity are from a Screener-derived aggregator and were not independently re-verified against the company's own filing — check on Screener for the latest figures before quoting precisely.
